title: Sidney Bechet, the Ivy League tour and his photography
summary: Rose says he toured the Ivy League with Bechet, Muggsy Spanier, Pops Foster and Baby Dodds, and recalls Bechet's obsession with cameras.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Yeah, we were talking about the first jazz concert. And talking about the people that were there. How well did you know Sidney Bichet? Oh, I knew him very well indeed. Because we made a tour of the Ivy League together, along with Muggsy Spanier and Pops Foster and Baby Dodds and various trombone players. Sometimes George Bruny's, sometimes Brad Gowans. Once later with Jimmy Archie.
You told me a lot of stories about Bichet, none of which come to mind right now.

Well, there are some interesting things. A lot of people that knew Bichet were aware of a period in his life when he got more interested in photography than in music. And I always felt like he was more interested in cameras than taking pictures. He used to come on a job with cameras hanging all over him like a Christmas tree and spend a lot of time shooting pictures of other musicians which never came out. And he was a very mild, quiet type of individual in all of my experience with him. Although he did sometimes become a little impatient with people, but he seemed to mask it well.
